messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] CDF of t-distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jens,

It looks like it’s missing from the R distribution collection. If I had time, I would implement it by forking the GitHub project, adding pt to distributions_R.hpp http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/distributions__R_8hpp_source.html
while using the other functions in that as examples/templates, then doing a pull request.

cheers,
Mollie

> On 31May 2019, at 23:00, Jens Wahl <jenschri...@hotmail.com> wrote:
>

> Hi,
>
> I trying to experiment with the skew t-distribution and by looking at the implementation from the sn package, its density has the following form:
>
> pdf(x) = dt(x) * 2 * pt(x), where pt is the cdf of the t-distribution. I can't see to find this function in TMB, so I'm wondering if anyone here has any tips on how to implement this in a good way?
>
> Thanks in advance!
>
> Jens
>

messages.subject: question about using UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t, why are my parameter estimates and nll.cov() different
messages.subject_clean: question about using UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t, why are my parameter estimates and nll.cov() different
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've attached really simple simulation script and cpp in hopes that someone might be able to explain why the parameter vector for the covariances and the parameters of the covariance matrix from the UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t object are different. Seems like based on my code they should be the same,

  PARAMETER_VECTOR(theta); //observation error
  UNSTRUCTURED_CORR_t<Type> nll(theta);

rep$theta == rep$'nll.cov'

Thanks,
Brandon

messages.subject: Writing auxiliary functions in separate files
messages.subject_clean: Writing auxiliary functions in separate files
messages.body_plain:
In order to organize my model code, I'd like to write some function to be used within my objective function in separate files. I've tried defining some simple functions in a header file and including it, but they were not available in my objective function.

Is it possible to split up a TMB program into pieces like this? Would it require changing the Makefile? My C++ knowledge is exclusively writing TMB models over the past two years, so I'm a bit out of my depth here. I am happy to be directed to general resources for C++ if I'm missing something basic.

If it matters, the model I'm developing is contained in an R package.

Thank you,

John Best

You should be able to. I find the stockassessment R package a good reference for building complex TMB models. It involves multiple C++ files and also has a great setup for passing around parameters by reference see https://github.com/fishfollower/SAM/tree/master/stockassessment/inst/include.
